title: Trajectory milestone matrix and eval dependencies for staged rollouts
creator: Sofia Morales
description: Goal: Create a practical, machine-readable milestone matrix that ties staged rollout 'trajectory' checkpoints to concrete eval dependencies and automated gates. This ticket defines the milestone cadence, required instrumentation, and the evaluation harnesses needed to run risk-weighted canaries for API surface changes and model/quantization swaps. Outcome: a checklist + JSON schema that SRE/Eng/PMs can import into the rollout orchestrator so rollouts are gated by slope, not just discrete thresholds.
milestones: M1 - Draft matrix and mapping to metrics (2025-11-20)
M2 - Instrumentation tickets created and assigned (2025-12-15)
M4 - Pilot canary using small customer cohort (2026-02-28)
M5 - Integrate into rollout orchestrator and publish schema (2026-03-15)
M6 - Full rollout gating + postmortem playbook (2026-04-12)
rollout_stages: stage-0: smoke (internal dev traffic only, 0% customer)
stage-2: limited cohort (5% selected customers, metrics tracking)
stage-3: ramp (progressive increase to 50% based on trajectory checks)
stage-4: GA (100% with continuous monitoring and fallback)
monitoring_signals: quality_signals: automated eval delta on anchor prompts
acceptance_criteria: Matrix covers at least 6 common experiment types: model swap, quantization, routing policy, batch config, cache warmup, and infra upgrade
Each milestone has at least one linked instrumentation ticket and one automated eval job
Rollout orchestrator accepts the schema and can abort or pause when slope-based gate fails
Pilot canary completed with no customer-facing regressions and documented roll-forward steps
Documentation published (Confluence) and on-call runbook reviewed by SRE
updates: 2025-11-10: Scoping meeting with Eng Reliability, Runtime, and Observability. Agreed to prioritize slope-based gates over single-threshold gates for noisy signals.
2025-11-22: PM/Eng agreed on initial metric set. Design asked to propose compact visualization for trajectory view. Assigned DES-214 to Design.
2025-12-08: ENG-1842 created to add model-level p99 tracing and per-request token counts. Estimated 3 sprints.
2026-01-18: Synthetic traffic harness prototype validated against KV cache warmup scenarios. Found warmup variance for large context models; mitigation added to milestones.
2026-02-02: Security review checkpoint passed in principle; final KMS-related gating will be separate. Security requested threat-model note for fallback artifacts.
2026-02-20: Pilot canary schedule confirmed. Slack channel #exp-rollouts created for live telemetry and escalation.
2026-03-01: Design provided mockups for trajectory dashboard; feedback included adding trend confidence band and ability to 'freeze' metric for postmortem analysis.
2026-03-08: Eng proposed two gate implementations: a fast conservative gate (lower false-negative) and an aggressive gate (faster ramp). PM prefers conservative for initial pilots.
2026-03-10: PR open for schema: github.com/redwood/rollout-orch/pull/482. Need integration test with canary harness before merging.
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Metric noise causes premature aborts. Mitigation: use slope and confidence intervals rather than single-sample thresholds, and require two consecutive failing windows before abort.
Risk: KV cache warmup variability skewing quality signals. Mitigation: include a warmup window in stage-1 and exclude first N requests from eval metrics.
Risk: Missing instrumentation blind spots for new models. Mitigation: dependency checkbox - model onboarding must include p99, token metrics, and eval anchors before staging.
Risk: Operational overhead for small experiments. Mitigation: provide templated matrices and default thresholds for common experiment types to reduce setup time.
